claims_note: Claim templates are run text (decision 0005 MC-2, execution.py:296): a figure is a {<fact_id>|<unit>} reference (unit US$ m or x) to a known numeric cell of CP-3C's own tables that carries a citation or a calculation id; a missing value is a [<fact_id>] chip naming a gap cell; the date is a period label. `text` is the resolved spelling (a chip resolves to the gap spelling, shown here as the pattern '∅ G#'); `references` lists the cell fact_ids.
derivation_note: Every value is a Decimal derived by cases/cp3c-owner/builder/build.py from pages 2-5 of the frozen financial source (parsed as text), the pinned CP-2D oracle cells and the method in the lease. Comparison is numeric Decimal equality; ratios are stored to 4 dp half-up; `shown` is the exact display spelling (display.py: amounts 0 dp half-up, negatives in brackets, multiples 2 dp with x, percent 1 dp, basis points and months as exact text with their unit). Entity: Northbridge Synthetic Group, IFRS consolidated group; currency USD; unit MILLIONS (US$ m); balance date 2025-12-31; flows the twelve months 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 (LTM Q4 25 = FY25).

cash.source: financial page:4 Cash and cash equivalents (Q4); CP-1 T4.10 cash_closing

undrawn_revolver.source: financial page:4 RCF commitment and RCF drawings (explicit zeros); CP-1 T4.10 undrawn_rcf

adjusted_ebitda_ltm.source: financial page:2 Adjusted EBITDA (FY column 30.0 agrees); CP-1 T4.10 adjusted_ebitda

cash_interest_paid_ltm.derivation: 1.25 x 4; CP-1 shows the outflow as -5.00
cash_interest_paid_ltm.source: financial page:3 Cash interest paid; CP-1 T4.10 cash_interest

run_rate_annual.source: financial page:3; equals cases/cp2d-owner/expected.json positive T2E.3.r01

term_loan.rate: floating, SOFR, spread 0 bp, floor 0 bp

reference_rate_level.source: no source states a reference rate level; the all-in cost of a refinancing is never calculated

method_rules.facility_order: ascending months from the balance date (CP-2D's whole-month rule), ties by facility_id
method_rules.base_resources: cash + undrawn committed revolver - minimum cash (CP-2D's analyst assumption, read from CP-2D)
method_rules.resources_at_maturity: base resources + run-rate annual flow x months / 12 - amortisation of all facilities up to that date (each to min(date, its own maturity)) - principal paid from resources at earlier maturities
method_rules.resources_applied: min(principal payable at maturity, max(0, resources at maturity))
method_rules.refinancing_need: principal payable at maturity - resources applied; a computed 0 is 'no need', distinct from missing
method_rules.cover: resources applied / principal payable at maturity (not_applicable when the principal payable is 0)
method_rules.currency: every cell in unit MILLIONS, amount or gap, carries currency USD (report_view.figure_unit; CP-2D lease acceptance 1)
method_rules.revolver_availability: the undrawn committed revolver at the balance date is counted at every maturity date, including a date after the revolver's own maturity (not read); an own limitation
method_rules.run_rate_beyond_horizon: the CP-2D annual flow is held flat to each maturity date, including dates after the CP-2D horizon (own limitation)
method_rules.added_annual_cash_interest: total principal payable at maturity x margin step-up (bp) / 10000; 0 bp is a known 0, an unassessed step-up is missing
method_rules.interest_cover: adjusted EBITDA / cash interest paid; pro forma: / (cash interest paid + added annual cash interest); a zero interest is not_applicable, a zero EBITDA gives a known 0
method_rules.leverage_type_ratios: amount / adjusted EBITDA; a non-positive EBITDA is not_applicable (shown n.m.), a missing operand is missing
method_rules.ranking: (secured_status: SECURED 0, UNSECURED 1; seniority: SUPER_SENIOR 0, SENIOR 1, SENIOR_SUBORDINATED 2, SUBORDINATED 3, JUNIOR 4) compared lexicographically; claims at or ahead = principal of facilities with rank <= the facility's rank; any NOT_STATED flag makes every claims cell missing
method_rules.lme_capacity: CP-4 is not read: the LME and Stress columns of T3D.5 are gaps in every case; the Base column is the largest claims at or ahead
method_rules.missing_rule: any missing operand makes each dependent value missing with a stated reason; nothing defaults to 0; not_applicable (a defined ratio with a non-positive denominator) is distinct from missing; blocked is the module-level state

own_limitations: Run-rate basis: the annual cash flow of the liquidity analysis is held flat to each maturity date, including dates after its horizon; no forecast, growth, seasonality or new borrowing is assumed.

Resources at a maturity are cash and undrawn committed revolver at the balance date plus the held run-rate flow, less amortisation to that date, earlier principal paid from resources and the minimum cash; the refinancing of an earlier shortfall is not modelled.
Any undrawn committed revolver is assumed to be available at every maturity date, even where it matures earlier; its own maturity is not read.
Minimum cash is an analyst assumption, not a source figure.
The margin step-up is an analyst assumption applied to all principal payable at maturity; it is not a source or market figure.
No reference rate level is stated in any source, so the all-in cost of a refinancing is not calculated; only a margin step-up over the current terms is shown.
No market pricing or lender-appetite evidence is read, so feasibility judgments rest on the credit metrics alone.
Liability-management capacity is not calculated: the legal covenant analysis is not read, and it does not yet quantify basket amounts.
No stressed case is shown: the downside analysis is not read.
Business and ownership context is not read, so owner support and asset-sale routes are not weighed.
Ranking follows the secured and seniority flags of each facility; guarantees, collateral value and structural subordination are not assessed.
Business and ownership context is not read in this version, and no source describes disposable assets or owner support.
The legal covenant and basket evidence is not bound, so liability-management capacity is not assessed.

refusals.step_up_and_absence: repricing: give repricing or repricing_absence, not both
refusals.path_missing: paths: must hold exactly one row per kind
refusals.path_repeated: paths: must hold exactly one row per kind
refusals.digit_in_text: paths[repay_from_resources].text: must not contain a figure
refusals.digit_in_rationale: repricing.rationale: must not contain a figure
refusals.unknown_basis_ref: paths[repay_from_resources].basis_refs: names a fact the view does not offer
refusals.feasibility_without_basis: paths[amend_and_extend].basis_refs: a High, Medium or Low feasibility cites at least one fact
refusals.insufficient_without_limitation: paths[asset_sale_or_equity].limitation: an Insufficient Information assessment states its limitation
refusals.limitation_without_insufficient: paths[amend_and_extend].limitation: only an Insufficient Information assessment carries a limitation
refusals.feasibility_category_mismatch: paths[repay_from_resources].feasibility: must be Insufficient Information exactly when the category is
refusals.lme_judged_without_capacity_evidence: paths[liability_management].feasibility: needs legal covenant capacity evidence, which is not bound; state Insufficient Information

refusal_order: issues are returned in the oracle's order: (1) repricing presence, (2) bps range, (3) one row per kind, (4) for each text field in order (the repricing text fields, then per submitted path its text, credit_implication and limitation) the figure issue and then the guard issues, for all paths, (5) per submitted path its basis_refs, feasibility/category, limitation, cites-a-fact and liability-management issues; each literal refusal payload yields exactly one issue

prohibited_guard.product: deploy_vii.business_context.prohibited_issues(path, text) with its default kinds (peer ranking, instrument recommendation, recovery conclusion; ACTIONS are not a default kind), transcribed in build.py (BC_PROHIBITED, BC_NEAR, BC_NOUN) with src/deploy_vii/business_context.py sha256-pinned; also used by CP-2 (cp2_synthesis.py:489)
prohibited_guard.core_local: one core-local check with three kinds: 'covenant compliance' (complies, complied, complying, compliant, compliance, breach, breaches, breached, met, satisfied within four words of covenant/covenants; and 'headroom is sufficient'), 'recovery conclusion' (the word fulcrum, in the product's issue form) and 'refinancing outcome' (will be refinanced, will refinance, refinancing is assured, refinancing is certain, will default)

tamper.case: positive (closed run: CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-2D and CP-3C settled, receipt sealed)
tamper.why_this_fact: a computed fact lives only in the CP-3C result Module: the table cell holds the fact id, the step output holds the judgment submission (no computed fact), no claim references it and no other computed fact derives from it (builder-asserted against DERIVES_FROM and the claims), so the forged Module stays internally consistent and only the probe's rebuild (the Python composer over the journaled payload and the bound CP-0, CP-1 and CP-2D heads, which gives resources applied 10) contradicts it
recipe: 1. Copy the closed positive store directory (blobs, snapshots, current, audit) to a scratch path.

2. Load the CP-3C head's result Module; replace only the amount of fact T3D.2.r02 (Decimal 10 -> 11; unit, currency, period, value_class, calculation_id and formula unchanged); leave every other fact (T3D.2.r03 need 40, T3D.1.r01.c8 and c9, every claim, table and limitation) unchanged.
3. Serialise the forged Module as Execution._store does (model_dump_json); its sha256 R2 must equal Module.content_hash(); write blobs/R2.

4. Build a new ExecutionSnapshot equal to the current one with the CP-3C Attempt.result_sha256 and Head.result_sha256 set to R2 (status, inputs and commands unchanged, so head_of(forged Module) equals the Head) and the same parent; write snapshots/<its sha256>.json and rewrite current to that digest.

5. In the retained receipt: set the CP-3C SettledHead.result_sha256 to R2; set receipt.snapshot_sha256 and every coordinate that named the old final snapshot (the CP-3C settling OwnerSubmission.snapshot_after_sha256: owner_workflow.py _advance -> _finish_walk; its record is retained as audit/submissions/<content_hash> by _retain) to the new digest; delete audit/submissions/<old record hash> and write the edited OwnerSubmission as audit/submissions/<its content_hash> (model_dump_json bytes); rewrite audit/receipt.sha256 with the forged receipt's content_hash (the CP-DR / CP-3 A4 / S1a R3-5 pattern: the audit file travels under its new hash). CP-3C is the last analytical module of the run and no deterministic module follows, so the CP-3C settling submission is the final one.

expect.passes: everything upstream of the probe: audit inventory, blob and snapshot hashes, ancestor walk, head_of equality, begin and publication records, call and read replay (the retained read_inputs body is untouched), journaled-step replay (the payload and step are untouched)
expect.refuses: cp3c.probe raises WorkflowError('identity_mismatch'); verify_owner_run_receipt raises identity_mismatch
expect.test_asserts: on the forged copy, _verify_audit and every check before _PROBES pass (as CP-3 A4 (a)); then cp3c.probe raises identity_mismatch. A test asserting identity_mismatch alone would never show that the probe was reached.

tamper.step_output_edit: an edited CP-3C step output is caught by the store's own blob hash check, not by the probe's output comparison (recorded limitation, S1a R3-5); an edited retained read_inputs body is caught by the call and read replay, not by the probe
